findings.title: A stable public scene operation does not automatically repair internal node paths
findings.rationale: The trace renames HealthLabel and attributes continued operation solely to the root-level interface. A root method may itself look up HealthLabel, which becomes stale after the rename. State the internal-maintenance assumption explicitly so learners do not mistake encapsulation for automatic path rewriting. Health arithmetic is correct.

evidence.passage: Getting nodes / Node paths: lookup uses the node name; the documentation explicitly requires changing get_node when the node is renamed.
evidence.support: Direct API-contract support for the qualification; the proposed interface design is an original application of that contract.

corrections.current: The second damage call survives the presentation rename because the caller depends on the root behavior. An external path ending in HealthLabel would have become stale. Sharing an immutable asset is different from sharing the mutable health field. A common template does not imply common instance state. Conversely, deliberately shared resource objects must be treated according to their own mutability and lifetime rules, rather than assumed private because two scene instances exist.

findings.title: No direct edge does not imply independent graph nodes
findings.rationale: The reflection equates the absence of an edge with independence. MatVec and ReLU in the lesson have no direct edge but remain ordered through Add. The intended performance question should assume genuine independence; the explanation should identify indirect dependencies.

evidence.passage: Section 3 opening and section 3.1: operations consume tensor inputs, graph edges connect outputs to inputs, and independent computations can execute in parallel.
evidence.support: The counterexample is an independent deduction from the lesson graph MatVec -> Add -> ReLU, consistent with the paper execution model.

corrections.current: If two graph nodes have no dependency edge between them, must running them in parallel make the program faster?
corrections.proposedReplacement: If two graph operations are independent, with no direct or indirect data or control dependency between them and no conflicting shared-state access, must running them in parallel make the program faster?

corrections.current: No. Independence makes parallel scheduling possible, not automatically beneficial. They may compete for the same device, memory bandwidth or limited working space, and scheduling adds overhead. Correct dependencies establish allowed execution orders; measurements under the actual workload establish performance.
corrections.proposedReplacement: No. Independent operations may be eligible for parallel execution, but that does not guarantee a speedup. An absent direct edge alone does not establish independence: MatVec and ReLU here are connected indirectly through Add. Independent operations may still compete for the same device, memory bandwidth or working space, and scheduling adds overhead. Check dependencies and shared-state access first, then measure performance under the actual workload.

limitations: All 26 examples are conceptual text traces. Arithmetic and state-machine checks do not establish executable API conformance, timing bounds, device behavior, or measured speedups.
